name: ai-automation
description: Multi-tenant Task Management SaaS backend API. Organizations can register, create projects, assign tasks to members, comment on tasks, attach files, receive notifications, and view audit logs and dashboards.

modules.name: Organizations
modules.description: Bootstrap new organizations. POST creates org + admin user + returns JWT access_token so the admin can immediately use the API. Public endpoint (no auth required).

modules.name: Auth
modules.description: User registration and login. Register creates a user with role='Member' (hardcoded, never from request body). Login validates credentials. Both return JWT access_token.

modules.name: Users
modules.description: User management for admins. List all users in tenant, get user by ID, update user profile, deactivate user. Admin-only for list/deactivate. Users can view and update their own profile.
endpoints: GET /api/users (Admin only - list all in tenant, with pagination)

modules.name: Projects
modules.description: Full CRUD for projects within a tenant. Only Admin and ProjectManager can create/update/delete. All authenticated users can list and view. Supports pagination and filtering by status.

modules.name: Tasks
modules.description: Full CRUD for tasks within projects. Any member can create tasks. Assignees and creators can update. Supports pagination, filtering by status/assignee/project, and search by title.
endpoints: GET /api/tasks (paginated, filter by status/project_id/assignee_id, search by title)

modules.name: Comments
modules.description: Comments on tasks. Any authenticated user can add a comment to a task. Users can delete their own comments. List comments for a task with pagination.

modules.name: Attachments
modules.description: File metadata for task attachments. Stores file_name, file_path, file_size (actual file upload is handled externally). Any user can attach to tasks they have access to.

modules.name: Notifications
modules.description: User notifications. System creates notifications when tasks are assigned, comments are added, etc. Users can list their own notifications and mark them as read.
endpoints: GET /api/notifications (own notifications, paginated, filter by read status)

modules.name: Audit
modules.description: Audit log for admin visibility. Logs all create/update/delete actions automatically. Admin can view audit trail with pagination and filtering by entity_type.
endpoints: GET /api/audit-logs (Admin only, paginated, filter by entity_type/user_id)

modules.name: Dashboard
modules.description: Dashboard statistics for the authenticated user's tenant. Returns counts and summaries.
endpoints: GET /api/dashboard/summary (total projects, tasks, users, tasks by status breakdown, recent activity)

database_tables: users (id, tenant_id, organization_id, email, password_hash, first_name, last_name, role, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
projects (id, tenant_id, organization_id, name, description, deadline, status, created_by, created_at, updated_at)
tasks (id, tenant_id, project_id, assignee_id, title, description, status, priority, due_date, created_by, created_at, updated_at)
comments (id, tenant_id, task_id, user_id, content, created_at)
attachments (id, tenant_id, task_id, uploaded_by, file_name, file_path, file_size, created_at)
notifications (id, tenant_id, user_id, type, message, read, entity_type, entity_id, created_at)
audit_logs (id, tenant_id, organization_id, user_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, metadata, created_at)

auth_rules.global_guards: JwtAuthGuard + RolesGuard + ThrottlerGuard registered as APP_GUARD in app.module.ts
auth_rules.public_routes: Use @Public() decorator — do NOT use @UseGuards() on any controller
auth_rules.req_user: jwt.strategy.ts validate() returns { id, email, role, tenant_id } — always use req.user.id, NEVER req.user.sub
auth_rules.register_role: ALWAYS hardcode role='Member' in auth.service.ts, NEVER accept role from request body

pagination_pattern.response_format: { data: T[], meta: { total, page, limit, totalPages } }

quality_requirements: Every module MUST have a controller with full REST endpoints
Every controller MUST have proper DTOs with class-validator decorations
Every service MUST filter by tenant_id on every query
Every list endpoint MUST support pagination
NEVER use @UseGuards() — guards are global via APP_GUARD
NEVER accept role from request body in register
All IDs are UUID v4, generated client-side with uuidv4()
Use snake_case for all database columns
Use camelCase for TypeScript properties in DTOs
Proper error handling with NotFoundException, ForbiddenException, ConflictException
Must compile with zero TypeScript errors
